newsitem.title: USA: Enron seeks constructive talks on Portland.
newsitem.headline: Enron seeks constructive talks on Portland.

text.p: Enron Corp is seeking constructive discussions with the Commissioners of the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (PUC) on its $2.1 proposed merger with Portland General Corp after the rejection of its rate reduction proposals by the staff of the PUC, a spokesman for Enron said.
"We look forward to making our case directly to the commissioners. Hopefully, they will realise that our offer is beneficial to Oregon," an Enron spokesman told Reuters.
The commission's staff rejected a rate reduction worth $61 million over three years for Oregon electricity consumers and is demanding that the two companies promise $141 million.
The case now moves from the staff of the commission to the commissioners themselves and Enron has said it will not hold any more discussions with the staff.
The Enron spokesman declined to comment on whether the two companies would offer the commissioners a better rate deal.
"I just cannot comment on that," he said.

Shares in Portland, which had fallen 7/8 in early trade, recovered to trade up 1/4 at 37-3/4 by 1336 EST/1836 GMT. Enron held on to gains earlier in the day and its stock was trading up 3/4 at 39-7/8. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
